official_sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
claims: The 1 metre LIDAR Composite DTM covers about 99 percent of England.
The DTM removes surface objects to represent terrain rather than buildings and vegetation.
The 2022 composite combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where repeat surveys exist the newest, best-resolution data is selected.
Bilinear interpolation is used where data is resampled before merging.
The composite includes surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
Downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5 kilometre tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevations are in metres referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn using OSTN15.
Input surveys have vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15 centimetres RMSE.
WCS, WMS, WMTS and metadata-index services have distinct delivery roles.
WCS GeoTIFF NoData pixels use the numeric value minus 3.4028235e+38.
Composite survey downloads include a GeoPackage spatial metadata index describing spatial location and temporal extent.

official_sources.authority: Environment Agency / Defra Data Services Platform
claims: Ground-truth points are independently surveyed and time-stamped survey products carry survey date, resolution, transformation and geoid metadata.
Post-August-2016 surveys use the OSGM15 geoid model according to the survey projection guidance.

quality_guards: Do not treat NoData as an elevation.
Do not mix DTM, last-return DSM and first-return DSM semantics.
Propagate survey date, resolution, datum, transformation and RMSE into every numeric result.
Keep TQ2892 candidate measurements blocked until exact filtered metadata and WCS raster bytes are read back.
